0.0.n: This borrowed word does not change form for plural groups.

0.1.n: 人 counts people; here it counts the group's members.

0.2.n: Links the seven members to うち, establishing the group from which three are selected.

0.3.n: のうち identifies a subset within a larger group.

0.4.n: 人 counts the members who were told about the prank.

0.5.n: Marks the three members as the topic of what follows.

1.0.n: Combines with 前日 to specify which event the previous day precedes.

1.1.n: 撮影前日 means the day immediately before filming.

1.2.n: Marks the time when the manager gave the information.

1.3.n: This borrowed word refers to the person managing the members.

1.4.n: Identifies the manager as the source of the information.

2.1.n: Combines with ドッキリ to describe a prank targeting people as they wake.

2.2.n: Often describes a hidden-camera surprise set up to capture someone's reaction.

2.3.n: Marks the wake-up prank as the thing that will take place.

2.4.n: Literally expresses existence; here the context makes it a future planned event.

2.6.n: Marks the preceding quotation as the content communicated to the members.

2.7.n: Passive 伝えられる plus ている shows they have already received the information.

3.0.n: ウソ means a lie, but here combines with 寝 to describe pretending to sleep.

3.1.n: This token crosses a word boundary: 寝 belongs to ウソ寝, while 人 begins 人狼.

3.2.n: 狼 completes 人狼, the werewolf game role used here for members secretly pretending to sleep.

0.lit: Among the seven members, as for three people,
0.tip: のうち means out of a group, so seven is the total and three is the subset.

1.lit: On the day before filming, from the manager,
1.tip: から marks who supplied the information, while に marks when it was supplied.

2.lit: Have been told, “There will be a wake-up prank,”
2.tip: と marks the quoted message, and the passive verb shows the members received it.

3.tip: Read this as ウソ寝 plus 人狼, regardless of the app's token split.
